text:
jess: quick heads-up — scheduling a short maintenance window in az3 TOMORROW 03:00-03:30 UTC. Plan: evacuate nodes with local NVMe, flush local caches, then graceful GPU resets on nodes with transient GPU driver errors. We'll do cohorts to avoid capacity cliffs.

infra-bot: calendar event created: 'az3 local-storage evac + gpu reset' 2026-03-21 03:00-03:30 UTC. Organizer: jess.

matt: which pools are affected? will this touch dedicated capacity or only spot backfill?

jess: primary: gpu.dedicated-az3 (capacity-sensitive) and gpu-spot-az3 as backfill. Default behaviour: cordon + evict pods on target nodes, rely on existing backfill but keep concurrency low.

sana: operational note — need to rsync local metadata (jobs checkpoint dir) to s3 before delete-local-data. Script in infra-tools: `scripts/evacuate_nvme.sh` does that but staggers deletes; tested in staging.

lee: we also have 3 nodes with NVMe SMART warnings (tagged `nvme-warn`). Prefer targeting non-warn nodes first and only reset warned nodes last.

jess: agreed. Selection: cohorts pick nodes without `nvme-warn` first. For SMART check we run `sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0 | grep 'critical_warning'` and treat >0 as candidate for manual intervention.

matt: quick cost calc — if backfill spins up full replacement VMs for all 30 nodes at once, worst-case egress + spot = ~ $1.8k/hr. Mitigation: reduce concurrency to 5 nodes per cohort, increase cohorts, extend window by 15m if needed.

sana: i vote for 5 concurrent. Also add a cache warmup step after each cohort: POST to internal warmup endpoint so model prefix cache repopulates before traffic hits. Example: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/warmup -d '{"models":["m-1","m-2"]}'`

oncall: i'll be oncall for the window. please @me if latency >200ms or available_gpus <95%. i'll have runbooks ready: `runbook/az-node-evac.md`.

jess: preflight checklist i'll run 15m before: 1) publish nodes list here; 2) run `kubectl get nodes -l region=az3 -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'`; 3) run a dry-run drain:`kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --dry-run=all`

lee: tested `evacuate_nvme.sh` in staging. Small tweak: add `--force` to `kubectl drain` for stuck daemonsets. pushed branch, PR: `git://repo/infra#234` (will merge after thumbs).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: job infra/local-evac-v1 queued — will run preflight checks 10m prior. Logs will be posted to /var/logs/infra/evac-1767777000.log.

matt: post-maintenance ops: disable autoscale-up for gpu.dedicated-az3 for 10m to avoid unexpected provisioning churn, monitor cost dashboard and set alert if spend delta > $200 in 30m.

sana: also ensure prefix cache TTL is short for this window in case we warm inappropriate entries. Setting TTL to 5m for warmup cycle.

jess: final plan (TL;DR): 5 concurrent nodes, cohorts until all targets drained (expect 6 cohorts), 5m spacing, rsync metadata -> s3, drain+evict with `--delete-local-data`, run nvme SMART check, graceful GPU reset only when driver errors present, warm prefix cache after each cohort, fallback route to `model-fallback` if available_gpus <90%. Posting node list 15m before window.

oncall: ack — will standby and run validation hooks. Pager policy active: page if p95 latency > 250ms or available_gpus <88%.

jess: thanks team :thumbsup: I'll post the node list and final run links shortly.
